findings.title: Crash when Meet location has no destination calendar
findings.body: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or an empty array, but the code dereferences `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration`. Any Google Meet event whose organizer has no destination calendar will throw before the Cal Video fallback can run. The previous code used optional chaining, so this is a regression; guard with `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration` or equivalent.

findings.title: Video references lose credentialId
findings.body: `referencesToCreate` now sets `credentialId` only for calendar results (`isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`). Non-calendar results are video meetings, and their `result.credentialId` is what lets later cancellation/update code find the video credential. With this change new video references have no `credentialId`, so deletion paths such as `handleCancelBooking` skip `deleteMeeting` and leave orphaned video meetings.

findings.title: Location updates create references without externalCalendarId or credentialId
findings.body: `updateLocation` now builds `referencesToCreate` using `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`, but `CalendarManager.updateEvent` never returns either field. As a result, after editing a location the newly created booking references omit `externalCalendarId` and `credentialId`, breaking future calendar updates/deletes and forcing legacy fallback behavior. The reference data must be taken from the update result/credential or from the event destination calendar.

findings.title: Google updateEvent loses destination-calendar fallback
findings.body: When `externalCalendarId` is not supplied, the `find` callback compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId`, which is `undefined` and therefore never matches a real destination calendar. The previous fallback used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. Updates for booking references that lack an external calendar id now send `calendarId: undefined` and fail instead of updating the selected destination calendar.

findings.title: Collective team destination calendars dropped when organizer has none
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. In that case `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op, so destination calendars collected from the other collective hosts are discarded. This means an organizer without a connected calendar prevents other hosts from receiving calendar invites, which is one of the cases this PR is meant to fix. Initialize the array and push unconditionally when team destinations exist.

findings.title: Office365 creates all events in the first host's destination calendar
findings.body: `createEvent` always uses the first element of `event.destinationCalendar` as the target calendar. `EventManager` now invokes `createEvent` once per destination with that host's credential, so the second Office365 host's credential is used against the first host's `externalId`. That creates the event in the wrong calendar or gets a Graph 404, and the second host is not properly invited. The target destination must be matched to the credential being used (or passed explicitly).

findings.title: Lark creates all events in the first host's destination calendar
findings.body: `createEvent` takes the first destination calendar from the array and ignores which credential called it. With multiple collective hosts, the second host's Lark credential will try to create the event in the first host's calendar id, so the event either fails or lands in the wrong calendar and the second host does not receive the expected invite. The service needs to select the destination corresponding to the credential used.

findings.title: CalDAV/BaseCalendar silently skips additional hosts
findings.body: `createEvent` filters available calendars down to the first destination calendar's `externalId`. When EventManager calls this service for the second host's destination, that externalId belongs to the first host's calendar and does not match any calendar for the second credential, so the filter returns an empty list and no event is created. Because empty responses are treated as success, the missing host event is silent. The filter should target the destination for the current credential rather than always the first array element.

findings.title: Recurring collective cancellations delete only one calendar reference
findings.body: The recurring cancellation branch still uses `updatedBooking.references.find(...)` and deletes only the first `_calendar` reference for each booking. With multi-host bookings there are now multiple calendar references, so only one host's recurring events are cancelled while the others remain on calendars. It also runs this work once per outer calendar reference, duplicating calls. It should iterate all calendar references for each updated booking.

findings.title: Organization slug condition appears inverted
findings.body: This unrelated change reverses the existing condition: previously `slug` was included only when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` was false, now it is included only when it is true. For self-hosted/no-billing installs, organizations will be created without a slug; for billing-enabled installs, they now get both a direct `slug` and `requestedSlug`, potentially assigning an unverified subdomain before the billing flow. Revert this or document why the condition should flip.
